pairs.why: The two are nearly the same, but A's thicker lens rims and plainer finish read a little more like the chunky real viewer, while B's lenses are glassier.
A has the chunky, glossy blue housing and soft toy-like shading of the real card, while B is a flatter, more realistic grey-faced viewer.
A's wide rounded silver face, big lenses and blue body are closer to the real card's chunky proportions than B's narrower, more realistic head.
A's smooth, saturated, chunky wood and large seeds match the real feeder better, even though B's two-point rope is closer to the real one.
A's simple open-post feeder hung on a two-point rope matches the real build better than B's arched walls and metal rings.
A keeps the plain chunky wood and rope hanging, while B adds a mechanical bracket, ring and rivets that the real feeder doesn't have.
B is built like a real calculator with labelled keys and cyan operator keys, while A's blank buttons make it read as a toy, even though A's blue keys match the real colour.
B has labelled number keys, cyan operators and the real card's smooth plastic finish, while A's blank keys don't look like a working calculator.
